purpose: The COMMENT on the live policy deals_uncontexted_read names its own reason for existing: 'while the export and analytics readers still run outside an RLS context'. This pass closes the analytics half. AnalyticsService.getUnitEconomics and getLedgerSummary had no tenant boundary at all - the second had no WHERE clause whatsoever - and ComplianceService.generateRegulatoryReport built a regulator-bound report from every tenant's deals. Removing the .catch handlers that hid this also unmasked a live BigInt arithmetic crash the same handlers were concealing from the type checker.
requiredInvariants: Role check stays first, before the tenant check and before any read, in both services. A caller whose role is not on the list must not learn about a missing tenant instead.

The tenant predicate is in the query. ANALYTICS_ROLES and EXPORT_ALLOWED_ROLES are the same four roles, and exports.service.ts already scopes all six of its reads for them; the boundary claimed here is that same one, not a new one.
An entry with no deal belongs to no tenant and is excluded. Same rule as the outbox pass; ledger_entries and disputes have no tenant column of their own.

Scope of the compliance change is named narrowly and not widened: only the DEAL read of generateRegulatoryReport. The KYC queue, audit log, sanction flags and organization reads of that service are a different table set, are NOT claimed closed here, and their remaining .catch handlers stay untouched.

No schema change, no migration, no RLS policy edit. deals_uncontexted_read is not dropped in this pass - it stays until the export readers are inside an RLS context too. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: getUnitEconomics, getLedgerSummary and generateRegulatoryReport each refuse a caller with no tenant, and refuse before any read.
getUnitEconomics filters deals by tenantId and counts disputes over exactly those deal ids, so the dispute rate cannot carry the platform's denominator.
getLedgerSummary, which had no WHERE clause at all, reads only ledger entries of the tenant's deals; an empty deal set yields an empty predicate rather than an unbounded read.

BigInt: totalKopecks and amountKopecks are BigInt in the schema. Measured in node, not reasoned: 0 += 100n raises TypeError: Cannot mix BigInt and other types. Regression tests hold real bigint values in the mocks, so they would pass on the old code if the mocks held numbers - they do not.

Thirteen mutations applied and all thirteen caught, each verified to have actually applied before the run: four tenant predicates dropped, three assertTenantScope calls removed, four .catch handlers restored, two BigInt conversions undone.
api typecheck exit 0 and the full @pc/api suite green.
